props.text: m lambda = d (sin i + sin theta). The face is the grating.
Experimental hall. One door holds the labs.
The pedestal cycles d and reflect/transmit. The card does not spin.
m lambda = d (sin i + sin theta)
m = 0 is the mirror. Color lives in m != 0.
One pedestal. The button cycles d and reflect/transmit. The card does not turn.
A grating is a periodic boundary. Period d. Order m. Wavelength lambda.
These rooms are benches, not a lock. Walk them in any order.
We use far-field (Fraunhofer) diffraction. Lasers are geometric. Scalar Kirchhoff, not RCWA.
1800 /mm makes 633 nm m=+1 vanish. sin theta > 1, the order dies.
Czerny-Turner: slit -> collimator -> grating -> camera -> exit slit.
Wider slit, more flux, worse d(lambda). R = mN. N is the illuminated width.
White light is many lambda. The grating maps lambda to theta. Linear in lambda, not n(lambda).
A prism disperses too. n(lambda) is not d.
Blaze angle theta_B. Facet is a tiny mirror. Littrow: i = theta = theta_B.
Holographic gratings are sinusoidal. Ruled can be blazed.
Periodic ruling error makes ghost orders. We do not simulate ghosts. Scalar code, not RCWA.
At a Rayleigh wavelength an order turns evanescent and efficiency jumps. You already saw vanish.
Echelle: coarse d, high m, high R. FSR at m=15, 532 nm is 35.5 nm.
High orders pack. A weak cross tilt separates them. The 532 m=15 pad only counts after the tilt.
Concave grating: Rowland circle. Entrance slit and spectrum share one circle.
Off the circle the 532 m=+1 order does not land. Walk the ring.
Pressed discs are gratings. Pit period ~1.6 um, about 625 /mm.
Balmer series. H-alpha 656.3 nm at 23.2 deg. H-delta 410.2 nm at 14.3 deg. 600 /mm, i=0, m=+1.
Fingerprint the lamp from the orders. Hydrogen is Balmer. Mercury is 435.8 / 546.1 / 578. Helium sits near 587.6 nm.
Read the HUD. Match the lines. Wrong pads do nothing.
D1 589.592 nm, D2 588.995 nm. R = lambda/d(lambda) ~ 1000. Wide slit fails. Narrow slit resolves.
m*lambda is what the grating sees. 2 x 400 nm = 1 x 800 nm. A 500-700 nm bandpass kills the blue second order.
S is brighter on this ruling
Scalar code cannot do full RCWA. We mix two efficiencies. Real gratings are vector. S is brighter on a typical ruling.
The grating works outside 380-780 nm. Your eye does not. Phosphor converts UV. A thermal plate converts IR.
A monochromator is a grating plus two slits. You are walking the selected lambda.
Littrow. i = theta = theta_B. 2 d sin(theta_B) = m lambda. Cycle to the 532 nm return.
You can leave. The card stays.
